config.title: FUNDA — Toast Notification Stack

intro.title: FUNDA — Toast Notification Stack
intro.body: In this lesson you will build a Toast Notification Stack — an overlay system that can push success, warning, and error toasts from anywhere in the application without touching the component tree. You will create a ToastService that imperatively creates and destroys ToastComponent instances using ViewContainerRef.createComponent(), manage a queue of active toasts, and auto-dismiss them after a configurable duration. This is the canonical example of service-driven dynamic component rendering that underpins modals, drawers, tooltips, and snackbars across enterprise UIs.
intro.usecase: Global notification systems exist in every enterprise application — form submission confirmations, background job status updates, real-time alert broadcasts. The pattern behind them (a service creates, manages, and destroys UI components programmatically) is the same pattern powering Angular Material's MatSnackBar, MatDialog, and CDK Overlay.

objectives: Inject ViewContainerRef into a service using the inject() function and understand why this requires a specific injection context
Dynamically create a ToastComponent instance using ViewContainerRef.createComponent() and pass data via componentRef.setInput()
Manage a stack of active toast references and implement FIFO or priority queue ordering
Auto-dismiss a toast after a configurable duration and destroy its ComponentRef to prevent memory leaks
Call the ToastService from any component, service, or HTTP interceptor using inject() without prop drilling
Style each toast variant (success, warning, error, info) using @Input bindings and conditional CSS classes
Implement ngOnDestroy on the ToastComponent to clean up any internal timers or subscriptions
